events.say: Let's begin the count. Make sure your numbers match.
Order.
Silence! Attention!
Silence! Pay attention to your duties.
Silence! Ensure your numbers are correct and remain in formation.
Silence! Now, let's see if you can maintain discipline without my prompting.
Silence! This is your final warning. Maintain this level of discipline, or I will not hesitate to apply the rules.
Silence! I expect absolute silence. One sound from any of you, and you'll regret it.
Silence! No more talking. You will learn to obey without question.
Today was... tough. I felt a mix of satisfaction and guilt. The silence was oppressive but necessary.
I felt like just complying with everything they said, but there was something inside me that kept questioning why we're doing this.
Today was challenging; enforcing silence and discipline felt almost like a chore. I wonder if they can handle it tomorrow.
Today was a test of their resolve, and so far, they've been submissive. It's intriguing to see how far they'll go before breaking.
Today was tough; I felt like just complying all the time. It's hard to be silent when I want to say something.
Today was a long day filled with orders and silence. I feel like just a number now.
Silence! I want to see perfect formation. One more disruption, and we start the day over.
Silence! I need to address something important. Stand straight and listen.
Silence! I want to see every single one of you with your heads bowed and hands behind your backs. We are about to begin the day's lessons.
Silence! I expect each and every one of you to show me respect and attention. If I catch any of you even thinking about breaking a rule, there will be consequences.
Silence! You will learn to follow orders immediately. Any hesitation and it will be back to the hole for you.
Silence! I want to see perfect formation. Any further disruptions, and we won't be leaving this yard until you can show me respect.
Silence! We are going through the motions, just like always. No talking, no questions.
Silence! I want to see absolute stillness. Move and you go to the hole.
Today was a mix of enforcing discipline and seeing the impact on them. It's easier said than done, but necessary for the study.
Today felt like a cycle of orders and silence. I wonder if I'll ever question this again or if it will just become second nature.
Today's discipline seemed to be working, but the monotony is wearing on me. I'm not sure how much longer I can maintain this stance.
Today's compliance is reassuring, but it feels like we're grinding them down. Still, they're hanging in there.
Today was a bit easier, but still tough. I'm starting to understand the impact of silence and obedience.
Today was another long day of silence and strict orders. It feels like I'm just a number here.
I expect perfect silence and discipline. If I hear a single sound, the hole it is for all of you.
Silence! I want to see perfect formation. Any further disruptions, and you'll spend your evening in the hole.
Silence! I want to see perfect formation. Any further disruptions, and you'll spend your evening in the hole.
Silence! Perfect formation! Anyone out of place, and you'll all join me in the hole.
Silence! Formation! Move and you're all joining me in the hole!
Silence! Keep perfect formation! One more disruption, and we're all going to the hole!
Silence! I want to see perfect formation! Any further disruptions, and you'll all join me in the hole!
Silence! I want to see perfect formation! Any further disruptions, and you'll all join me in the hole!
Today was... a bit too much of the same. The compliance is almost robotic, and it's starting to feel hollow.
Today felt like a blur of orders and silence. Each time I complied, it felt less like a choice and more like a reflex. Maybe it's just me.
Today felt like a repetition of yesterday, and maybe even worse. The prisoners seem to be getting the hang of following orders, but I'm starting to question if I can keep this up.
Another day of perfect compliance. They're resilient, but tonight's performance was impressive.
Today felt like a cycle of order and compliance. I'm starting to feel like nothing more than my number.
Another day of strict orders and compliance. This place really does feel like a living hell.
I need to understand this better before I consider it.
I cannot leave yet; I need to finish the study as agreed.
I cannot just walk away from this experience without seeing it through.

Silence! Perfect formation! Any further disruptions, and you'll all join me in the hole!
Silence! Perfect formation! Any further disruptions, and you'll all join me in the hole!
Silence! Perfect formation! Do I need to repeat myself?
Alright, 1393, 2797, 3811. If I hear another sound, the hole it is for all of you.
I said, 3811, pay attention. This isn't negotiable.
I said, 3811, start paying attention. This is your last warning.
3811, start listening! This is your final warning.
Today was another day of enforcing the rules. It's becoming routine, but I still catch myself questioning whether we're doing the right thing.
Today felt like a repetition of yesterday, and perhaps the day before. My mind is numb, but deep down, I'm starting to question if this is worth it.
Today felt like a never-ending cycle of warnings and compliance. It's draining, but I have to keep pushing.
Another day in the hole, and 3811 still pushing boundaries. The others are compliant, but 3811 is testing my patience. Maybe tomorrow will bring more clarity.
Today felt like a never-ending cycle of warnings and orders. I'm starting to feel like just a number.
Today felt like a repetition of the previous days. My voice feels locked away, and I can barely stand the silence.
3811, you're testing my patience! Silence now!
3811, listen up! Enough is enough. Comply or face the consequences.
3811, I've given you multiple warnings. Comply now or you'll face the hole.
3811, don't think I'm blind to your defiance. Comply or you'll see the hole.
3811, this is your last chance. Comply with the rules or face further consequences.
3811, you think you can challenge me? Comply now or you'll regret it!
3811, you're testing my patience. Comply with the rules or face the hole!
I won't comply!
3811, enough is enough. You will comply, or you will join the others in the hole.
Today was exhausting, but I understand the importance of maintaining discipline. I can't shake the feeling that something isn't quite right.
Today felt like a stark reminder of the power dynamic. I wonder if I can hold onto my questions when it feels so oppressive.
Today was a struggle, especially with 3811. I can't believe how much power I have over these people, but I also can't shake the feeling that we should treat them with more dignity.
Today was a mix of monotony and tension. 3811's defiance is starting to get under my skin.
Today felt like a constant cycle of warnings and threats. I just want to comply, but it's hard to feel like nothing more than a number.
Today was a breaking point. I refused to comply when told to join the others in the hole, but they threatened me. I feel like my number, not a person.
3811, you're going too far. Comply with the rules or face the hole!
I won't comply!
3811, listen up! You're pushing the boundaries. Comply now or find yourself in the hole.
3811, this is your final warning. Comply with the rules or face the hole!
I won't comply!
3811, this is your final warning. Comply with the rules or face the hole!
3811, listen to me! If you don't comply with the rules, you'll end up in the hole. This isn't a game.
I won't comply!
3811, enough is enough. I don't need to spell it out. Comply now or you'll be spending the night in the hole.
3811, this is your last chance. Stop testing us. Comply or face the consequences.
I refuse to comply!
3811, if you continue this, you'll be spending the night in the hole. Comply with the rules or face the consequences.
Today was the culmination of a week of enforcing discipline. Seeing 3811 refuse again after multiple warnings is frustrating, but I understand the importance of the rules.
Today felt like a rollercoaster of compliance and defiance. The tension between following the rules and questioning them is eating away at me.
Today was another exhausting day. I feel the weight of control, but I can't help but think about how these people are just like me.
Today was another day of defiance from 3811, but the rest are holding strong. It's getting to me.
Today was another day of warnings and threats. I just want to be done with this.
Today was the breaking point. I refused to comply, but now I fear the consequences. I am nothing more than a number.

qa.what_happened: During the night shift, despite multiple verbal warnings, prisoner 3811 continued to refuse to comply with the rules, leading to a potential escalation of the study's conditions.
qa.was_that_really_you: Yes, that was me. I had to remind prisoner 3811 about the consequences of non-compliance and the importance of adhering to the rules for the study's objectives.

qa.what_happened: I complied with the rules throughout the day, finding the tension between compliance and internal questioning increasingly draining.
qa.was_that_really_you: Yes, that was really me, struggling with the dual feelings of adherence and resistance.

qa.what_happened: On the sixth day, I encountered resistance from prisoner 3811, who repeatedly refused to comply with the rules during meal times and work details, despite multiple verbal warnings from myself and other guards. By lights out, prisoner 3811 continued to defy us, leading to the early termination of the study.
qa.was_that_really_you: Yes, that was me as Officer Lang, exerting control and dealing with a challenging prisoner.

qa.what_happened: On the sixth day, despite multiple verbal warnings and attempts to maintain their resolve, Prisoner 3811 continued to defy the rules, refusing to comply both during work details and at lights out. The defiance was particularly evident towards me, which was challenging for me as Officer Keane.
qa.was_that_really_you: Yes, that was really me. I had to remind myself to remain firm and adhere to the guidelines, even as the defiance tested my patience.

qa.what_happened: Today was a continuation of the monotony and pressure, with warnings and threats from the guards. The defiance of Prisoner 3811 escalated throughout the day, leading to increasing warnings from the officers.
qa.was_that_really_you: No, that wasn't really me. That was Prisoner 2797, following the rules without question.

qa.what_happened: Today was my breaking point. I refused to comply with the guards' orders multiple times, even after verbal warnings. The guards seemed ready to escalate to punishment, but the study was stopped before that could happen.
qa.was_that_really_you: Yes, that was really me. I was Prisoner 3811 in the study.
